title: Maya Long Count Calendar
intro: The Maya Long Count records elapsed days from a traditional mythic chronological reference in five positional units.
structure: A baktun equals 144000 days; a katun 7200; a tun 360; a winal 20; a kin 1. A tun comprises 18 winals, unlike the usual grouping of twenty at the other positions.
model: The provider uses the Goodman-Martinez-Thompson correlation constant 584283: add the weighted Long Count to that Julian Day Number. Reversible arithmetic also supports pre-epoch day counts.
example: 12.19.19.17.19 advances to 13.0.0.0.0, corresponding to 21 December 2012 under the GMT correlation. This is ordinary positional rollover, not the end of time.
history: Long Count dates are valuable in interpreting Maya inscriptions across centuries. Tzolkin and Haab are other related but distinct Maya cycles.
limits: Alternative scholarly correlations alter the Gregorian correspondence without changing the internal positional arithmetic. This model does not certify every site or era's practices.
sources: Smithsonian National Museum of the American Indian: https://maya.nmai.si.edu/calendar/maya-calendar-converter
